options: Monthly sales that grow by about 1.5 units every month
A random walk, where each value is the previous value plus a random step
A series with a December spike that repeats every year, with the level otherwise unchanged
White noise: random values with a constant mean and spread and no dependence on the past
questions.explain: Trend, a random walk's wandering level, and seasonality each make the mean depend on time. White noise has constant mean and variance.

questions.q: What is the null hypothesis of the ADF test?
options: The series has a unit root (it is non-stationary)
The series is stationary
The series has no missing values
The series has a seasonal period of 12
questions.explain: ADF starts by assuming non-stationarity, so a small p-value is evidence the series is stationary. KPSS uses the opposite null.

questions.q: In the lesson, the ADF p-value for the random walk was 0.307. What does that mean?
options: The walk is definitely stationary
There is not enough evidence to reject non-stationarity, which fits a random walk
The test failed to run
The walk has exactly 30.7% noise
questions.explain: A large p-value means we cannot reject the null of a unit root. Differencing the walk gave p of 0.000.

questions.q: After first-differencing the monthly sales series, the ADF test said stationary, yet the ACF at lag 12 was 0.70. What does this suggest?
options: The test result is always correct, so ignore the ACF
Differencing added a trend
A seasonal pattern is still present, so seasonal differencing is worth trying
The series has too many observations
questions.explain: ADF tests for a unit root, not for seasonality. The spike at lag 12 in the ACF shows a yearly pattern remains.

questions.q: What does seasonal differencing with s.diff(12) do on monthly data?
options: Subtracts the previous month from each value
Removes the first 12 months only
Averages each year
Subtracts the value from the same month a year earlier, removing a stable yearly pattern
questions.explain: s.diff(12) compares each value with the one 12 periods earlier, cancelling a seasonal pattern that repeats at that period.
